nodes.title: Qubits and Superposition
nodes.conceptSummary:
In classical computing, a bit is strictly either 0 or 1. A quantum bit (qubit) is a two-state quantum-mechanical system described as a linear superposition:
$$|\psi\rangle = \alpha |0\rangle + \beta |1\rangle$$
Where $\alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{C}$ and $|\alpha|^2 + |\beta|^2 = 1$. The fundamental invariant is that measurement collapses the superposition into a definite state with probability $|\alpha|^2$ or $|\beta|^2$.

conceptualVariants.content: The fundamental invariant is that measurement collapses the superposition into a definite state with probability $|\alpha|^2$ or $|\beta|^2$.

proceduralPerturbations.expectedBoundaryBehavior: "Measurement collapses the equal superposition (1/sqrt(2)|0> + 1/sqrt(2)|1>) into |0> with 50% probability and |1> with 50% probability."

nodes.title: Unitary Operations and Reversibility
nodes.conceptSummary:
All quantum logic gates operating on closed systems must be represented by unitary operators $U^\dagger U = I$.
Because unitary transformations preserve the inner product and norm of vectors, all quantum computation without measurement is strictly reversible. No quantum gate can perform irreversible erasure of quantum information without increasing thermodynamic entropy.

conceptualVariants.content: All quantum logic gates operating on closed systems must be represented by unitary operators $U^\dagger U = I$.

nodes.title: Quantum Entanglement and Non-Locality
nodes.conceptSummary:
Entanglement occurs when a multi-qubit system cannot be factored into the tensor product of individual qubit states:
$$|\Phi^+\rangle = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(|00\rangle + |11\rangle)$$
Measuring the first qubit immediately forces the state of the second qubit, regardless of spatial separation. The core invariant is that entanglement does not allow faster-than-light communication because local marginal probabilities remain invariant.

conceptualVariants.content: The core invariant is that entanglement does not allow faster-than-light communication because local marginal probabilities remain invariant.

proceduralPerturbations.probe: If boundary inputs invert, how does Quantum Entanglement and Non-Locality preserve state?
proceduralPerturbations.expectedBoundaryBehavior: "Alice cannot transmit information faster than light because Bob's local marginal probability remains exactly 50/50 until classical measurement correlations are communicated."
